messages:
jess: FYI — Escalation from Acorn Apps. They report streaming responses getting truncated on final tokens and a pile of client reconnects. They say the client sees a 200 SSE stream with partial last event then connection closed and subsequent 499s. They attached a quick repro and logs, asking for a short-term workaround and root cause. :eyes:

jess: Repro summary from customer (copied):
```
# client: curl --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/resp?key=REDACTED
# server sends some events then: `tcp FIN` immediately after last event. client reconnects -> 499.
request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
last_event_id: 98765
```

matt: Can you paste the server logs around req_0a1b2c3d? Also which infra is in front of them (ALB / GCLB / Nginx / Fastly)? 499s usually means client closed, but abrupt FIN after event implies proxy idle or probe.

jess: Logs (snippet):
```
[2026-06-04T12:11:02Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d state=streaming event_count=12 bytes_sent=12345
[2026-06-04T12:11:17Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d send_event id=98765 chunk=...
[2026-06-04T12:11:17Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d connection=client_fin reason=remote_close
```
Client stack (customer):
```
EventSource.onmessage -> processes partial payload -> sudden connection error -> reconnect
```

lin: Important details: many edge proxies/tcp proxies will close idle connections if they don't see data for a timeout window. SSEs that rely on long gaps between events need heartbeats. Common patterns: send a comment ping like `: ping\n\n` every 15s, or a zero-length comment. Also ensure upstream proxies have `proxy_read_timeout`/idle timeout > heartbeat interval. What front are they using?

acorn-customer: They sit behind a managed Nginx reverse proxy (our infra) and we use default proxy_read_timeout=60s. We were sending events ~70s apart in low-traffic periods.

matt: That lines up. If events are >60s apart Nginx will close and tear down with FIN, server/runtime may log connection close right after last send. Quick mitigation: enable comment pings from server at 15s. Also set `Connection: keep-alive` and try `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`.

support-ops-bot: Runbook snippet: https://intranet.redwood/ops/sse#keepalives — quick repro command: `curl --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/resp` (use --no-buffer to observe comment pings). Capture with `tcpdump -i any -w sse.pcap port 443` for tcp-level verification.

jess: Customer tried adding comment ping at 30s but still saw disconnects. They pasted their Nginx config: `proxy_read_timeout 60s; proxy_send_timeout 60s;` — they increased to 120s temporarily and reported fewer disconnects but still occasional cutouts during bursts.

lin: 30s might be borderline if there's intermediate LBs (ALB idle default 60s) plus other timeouts. We should standardize to 15s heartbeats for our runtime by default, and allow override. Proposed plan:
- server: emit `:ping\n\n` every 15s when no events in flight
- server: include `Retry: 5000`? (client-side reconnect advice)
- support: document recommended upstream timeouts (>= 30s) and example Nginx config
- client: advise resume with `Last-Event-ID` and exponential backoff with jitter

matt: Also add `last_event_id` support in our SDKs so ephemeral reconnection resumes are reliable. For now, customer can send `Last-Event-ID: 98765` header on first reconnect attempt or rely on EventSource's `Last-Event-ID` semantics.

billing-bot: Not seeing any anomalous billing spike from this customer — traffic is low. Warn: if they reduce reconnect backoff aggressively it could increase cost. Suggest rate-limiting recon attempts server-side for anonymous endpoints.

jess: I asked Acorn to capture a tcpdump and to try our repro script that uses `--no-buffer` and `--header 'Accept: text/event-stream'`. I also told them to temporarily set Nginx `proxy_read_timeout 180s` and roll our 15s heartbeat canary.

support-ops-bot: Canary plan created in `support/canaries/1945123456` and pinged @oncall for a brief window.

deploy-bot: rolled config: runtime heartbeat interval set to 15s on canary-hosts at 1946-06-05T03:00Z. rollid=canary-1945123456

lin: Client guidance snippet (JS):
```
const es = new EventSource(url);
let lastId = null;
es.onmessage = e => { lastId = e.lastEventId || lastId; /* process */ };
es.onerror = () => { /* exponential backoff reconnect */ setTimeout(() => new EventSource(url + (lastId ? `?last_event_id=${lastId}` : '')), backoff); }
```
Add jitter and cap to prevent stampede.

matt: Action items: (1) Support: verify tcpdump when provided, (2) Runtime: enable 15s comment pings by default and add config toggle, (3) SDK: docs and Last-Event-ID helper, (4) Support: recommend upstream timeouts >= 90s for customers who can't add heartbeats quickly.

acorn-customer: Thanks — we will test tomorrow after you push canary. If we still see abrupt FINs we'll provide pcap.

jess: I'll follow up after canary results. tagging this as P1 until we have 24h without disconnects. :thumbsup:

(moderation) Note: thread contains snippets from customer logs and a request-id; sensitive keys were redacted.
